newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PBL sees yr EBIT ahead of previous yr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PBL sees yr EBIT ahead of previous yr.

text.p: Media group, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd said on Wednesday it anticipated its earnings before interest in tax would be slightly higher in the year to June 30, 1997 compared to the previous year.

"Our television and magazines divisions continue to operate in a very soft advertising market, with little prospect of any significant improvement in the second half of this financial year. Accordingly, the group overall should end this financial year in EBIT terms slightly ahead of last year," PBL managing director James Packer said in a statement.

Packer said PBL's television division earnings were likely to be flat, on a year on year basis, in the second half as a result of increased costs associated with the additional movies becoming available with the expiry of the first year of the pay television window.
Earlier PBL reported a 3.1 percent fall in its net profit for the six months to December 31 to A$104.30 million.
Earnings before interest, tax and abnormals rose 2.5 percent to A$178.8 million for the half, while earnings per share fell 3.2 percent to 20.53 cents.
There was a A$12.2 million abnormal gain in the first half of 1995/96 and no abnormals in the first half of 1996/97.
Sales fell 2.2 percent to A$581.6 million.
PBL said television revenue fell 1.5 percent to A$326.1 million, but the latest half was for 26 weeks against 27 weeks in the previous comparable half.
PBL's television division increased EBIT for the half by 1.1 percent to A$106.7 million, while the magazine division increased EBIT by 0.2 percent to A$63.1 million.
The enterprises division raised EBIT to A$9.0 million from A$5.9 million a year earlier.
"Magazines will start to feel more fully the impact of reduced paper prices and will post a significant increase in earnings over last year's second half," Packer said.

EBIT from the enterprises division would fall in the second half because no dividends were expected from PBL's stake in Hollywood movie group Regency Enterprises because shareholders had decided they would be reinvested in future.
